div.head: Hu 2.1
div.ab: ⁊ sylle mon þæt ceapgyld ðam ðe þæt yrfe age; ⁊ dǽle man þæt oðer on twa: healf ðam hundrede, healf ðam hlaforde — butan mannum; ⁊ fo se hlaford to ðam mannum.
Et reddatur ceapgildum ei cuius pecus erat (est); et reliquum dividatur in duo: dimidium hundredo, dimidium domino —preter homines, et habeat eos dominus suus.

Possessori autem sue rei precium reddatur de rebus, si forte res ipsa furto ablata periit; residuum uero in duo diuidatur: et quidem dimidium cadat in ius et possessionem tocius centenarii, dimidium uero in ius domini — preter homines (uel familiam), qui soli domino contingant.
⁊ sylle mon þæt ceapgyld ðam ðe þæt yrfe age; ⁊ dǽle man þæt oðer on twa—healf ðam hundrede, healf ðam hlaforde—butan mannum; ⁊ fo se hlaford to ðam mannum.

Und man zahle [aus Diebesgut] das Ersatzgeld dem Eigenthümer des [gestohlenen] Viehs; und man theile das Übrige in zwei [Hälften]: halb der Hundertschaft, halb dem Herrn [des Diebes] — ausser den untergebenen Leuten [des Diebes]; nämlich diese Untergebenen erhalte der Herr [alle].

And let the compensation-money [from the thief's goods] be paid to the owner of the [stolen] cattle; and let the rest be divided in two [halves]: half to the hundred, half to the lord [of the thief] — except for the [thief's] dependants; namely, let the lord receive these dependants [all].

And the value of the livestock shall be paid to its owner, and the remainder [of the thief's property]—all except his men—shall be divided in two, half [being given] to the hundred, and half to his lord who shall also take over his men.

And the value of the stolen property is to be given to him who owns the cattle, and the rest is to be divided into two, half for the hundred and half for the lord—except the men; and the lord is to succeed to the men.

Dies wiederholt dem Sinne nach III Eg 7 = II Cn 25, 1 = Leis Wl 47, 1
III Eg 7 = II Cn 25, 1 = Leis Wl 47, 1 repeat this in substance
Der Zusatz in Cons nimmt, wie IV Eg 11, o. II S. vii berichtigt, den regelmässigen Fall an, dass der Dieb das gestohlene Vieh geschlachtet hatte
The addition in Cons assumes, like IV Eg 11 (as corrected above II p. vii), the usual case in which the thief had slaughtered the stolen cattle

Der Herr ist hier und c. 3 nicht regelmässig der König, auch nicht (wie Maitland Domesday 287 meint) der Hundredherr, der wohl damals noch selten war und sich gerade den Justizertrag des Hundred zuerst nahm, sondern wie in c. 7 der persönliche Herr des Beklagten, mit Strafgeldempfang

The lord here and in c. 3 is not as a rule the king, nor (as Maitland Domesday 287 thinks) the lord of the hundred, who was probably still rare at that time and who took precisely the judicial revenue of the hundred first, but, as in c. 7, the personal lord of the accused, who receives the fine

Dieser Strafgeldempfang des Herrn musste das Institut des Gefolges (s. d. Gl 21) stärken und die private Gerichtsbarkeit (s. d. Gl 20a. b) fördern. Neben Unfreien (s. d. Gl 23c) können vielleicht [laut Analogie mit testamentarischer Verfügung über Gefolgsleute] auch kommendierte Untergebene des Diebes gemeint sein; in diesem Falle wurden sie nur unmittelbares Gefolge des Herrn, ohne Freiheit einzubüssen

This receipt of fines by the lord was bound to strengthen the institution of the retinue (see that word in Gl 21) and to promote private jurisdiction (see that word in Gl 20a. b). Besides the unfree (see that word in Gl 23c), commended dependants of the thief may perhaps also be meant [by analogy with testamentary disposition of followers]; in that case they merely became the immediate followers of the lord, without losing their freedom
Cons. Cn. adds si forte res ipsa furto ablata periit.
